ideas.truth: We trust water that tastes like it came from someone who loved us, not from a brand that tells us it's pure.
ideas.moment: The instant you notice a copper bottle on your own kitchen ledge doing exactly what your Dadi's matka used to do overnight.
ideas.key_frame: A sharp, sunlit copper bottle in the foreground; a soft, blurred copper matka echoing behind it — old and new doing the same job.

ideas.truth: Modern mornings are rushed — the rituals that took care of us quietly get dropped, not rejected.
ideas.moment: A working person grabs the copper bottle off the counter along with keys and tiffin, on the way out the door.
ideas.key_frame: Copper bottle standing between a bunch of keys and a steel tiffin box, morning light slicing across a small kitchen counter.

ideas.truth: Some objects earn a place on the shelf simply because they carry care in their material, not their marketing.
ideas.moment: The bottle sits alone on a windowsill at golden hour, exactly where a family's copper vessel would have once caught the same light.
ideas.key_frame: A single copper bottle on a sunlit windowsill, dust motes drifting through a shaft of late-afternoon light, nothing else in frame.

why: It directly answers the customer's own headline (Dadi's water) and follows the craft note to sell against home-made ritual rather than rival brands — the matka-echo does the persuading, so the ad needs no invented claims. A single key at the base now borrows the 'rushed morning' tension from Idea 1 for scale and context, without cutting Idea 1's own moment from the record.
treatment: We open on a single still: a copper bottle on a wooden window ledge in soft, low morning light, a bead of condensation caught mid-slide down its neck. Beside its base, a single brass door key rests casually — the kind grabbed on the way out — giving the eye a familiar object for scale and a whisper of the rushed morning it survives. Behind the bottle, out of focus, is the ghost of a copper matka — the vessel every Indian household once kept water in overnight so it would taste right by morning. The bottle sits in sharp, warm focus; the matka is a memory, not a subject. Near the base of the cap, a faint engraved wordmark catches the same highlight edge as the condensation bead — visible on close look, not shouting. No hands, no faces — just the quiet exchange between old and new doing the same job. Warm rose-gold tones, one soft highlight, one honest shadow. Above the bottle, calm open light carries the headline in Hinglish: 'Paani, jaise Dadi rakhti thi.' Below, price and brand sit in the same calm space: Tamra, Pure Copper Bottle 1L, ₹899.

scenes.prompt: An Instagram product photo of a tall pure copper water bottle with a polished rose-gold surface and matching screw cap bearing a faint engraved wordmark, standing on a wooden window ledge in warm morning light. A condensation droplet slides down its shoulder. A brass door key rests at its base for scale, with a soft blurred copper matka glowing behind it. Shallow depth of field, warm golden tones, calm empty space top and bottom for text overlay.

finish.copy_placement: Headline 'Paani, jaise Dadi rakhti thi.' sits in the calm top-third light band above the bottle; 'Tamra · Pure Copper Bottle 1L · ₹899' sits as a single calm line in the bottom-third band, set in the brand's own typeface for legibility over mood, checked against the dimmest patch of the wood/light behind it.
finish.end_card: No separate end card — this single static frame is both hero shot and end frame; product stays sharp and centred with copy resting in the pre-planned calm bands.
finish.music: Not applicable — this is a static Instagram feed image, no audio component.

decisions.D1_idea: The exact moment a copper bottle on today's kitchen ledge quietly does what Dadi's copper matka always did overnight.
decisions.D2_conflict: Modern homes have dropped the copper-matka ritual for convenience (plastic/steel bottles), losing the taste and trust that ritual gave, without anyone deciding to reject it. The rushed-morning key at the base signals this without adding a second scene.
decisions.D3_roles: Hero: the person who grew up drinking Dadi's copper-kept water but now defaults to plastic; Tamra is the guide/enabler that takes over the chore of copper-storage while keeping the valued tradition alive.
decisions.D4_opening: A bold, sharp close-up: the copper bottle mid-frame with a single condensation droplet frozen on its shoulder, immediately readable as 'fresh, cool water' — no build-up needed since it's a single still.
decisions.D5_brand: The product now carries its own faint engraved wordmark near the cap base, in addition to the text overlay — so the asset is ownable even if screenshotted without the text band.
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: The ask (buy at ₹899) is carried entirely by on-screen text; native Instagram feed CTA button handles the explicit next-step action at the platform level. The final frame is the product itself, sharp, centred, with copy resting in its pre-cleared calm bands.
decisions.D7_product_truth: Cylindrical bottle shape, pure-copper rose-gold colour, screw cap with a small engraved wordmark, roughly 1L-proportioned silhouette (now scaled visually against a everyday brass key) — all consistent with the customer's own words ('pure copper bottle 1L'); no invented features beyond this.
decisions.D8_deviations: Treating the brief as a static single-frame Instagram photo, not a multi-scene film, because the customer explicitly asked for a feed ad (photo) and the media model (Nano Banana 2) is stills-only. Added a key (scale + rushed-morning cue) and an engraved wordmark (brand ownership) to close checklist gaps — without deleting or replacing any previously described moment or motion cue (condensation, matka-echo both retained as originally written). Image prompts describe the wordmark generically (no literal brand text) since on-screen copy, including the brand name, is composited by code rather than rendered by the image model.
